findings.where: Motion section at the foot of the sheet: the full-width lavender panel behind the curve, Mark's repeated line and the timing table (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: A large, saturated lavender ground appears that is not in the declared palette and has no job. It is the loudest surface on the page and a third hue on a direction meant to be warm paper with blue and grey as the only ink. It also puts the blue 'Replay the entrance' link and the blue curve on an undeclared ground.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief for v1 calls for one soft ground and the house blue and grey only, with yellow as the single colour memory. A lilac slab makes the tile read as a different, more playful brand. Mark would object for the same reason: he wants it refined, never childish.

findings.where: Palette section: the four swatches (Counsel's paper, Logo grey, Logo blue, Pad yellow)
findings.fault: Four like swatches each get a different surface treatment: a square-cornered rectangle with a hairline, a rounded filled rectangle, an ellipse, and a square rectangle with a heavy blue border. Nothing in their roles calls for the difference, so the specimen reads as careless. It also implies that rounded corners and blue borders belong to the system, when the texture note says every corner is square.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who reads the palette specimen as the system's own statement. Mixed shapes and edges undercut a direction whose whole claim is restraint and one consistent document edge.

findings.where: Pad yellow: listed in the palette as 'the address strip' and described as sitting 'at the foot of the sheet', but on the page it appears only as a small bar inside the texture swatch
findings.fault: The one accent colour the direction is built on never appears on the page as a surface. No contact panel or quotation sits on the yellow, so the legal-pad memory exists only in the specimen. The first screen and the article are plain paper and grey alone.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for the legal pad to be saved with care as a pale yellow behind one quotation or the contact panel. Without it the tile loses its one borrowed detail and moves towards the 'dull' house-colours result he rejected.

findings.where: Article page: the lectern photograph set on a solid dark-grey block filling the column width (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The article image sits on a heavy flat slab close to the logo grey. It is the darkest large surface on the sheet and breaks the quiet paper ground. It also goes against the tile's own palette note that photographs are multiplied onto the paper so their backdrops take its warmth.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's article, who meets a dark block that weighs more than the text around it. The founder would object too, because the tile's stated surface rule is not held on the very page meant to prove it.
